gaps.title: On Sundays, 22,661 people have no bus or train within 800 m before 6:30 am
gaps.detail: 212 stops get their first trip after 6:30 am on Sunday 15 November 2026. Routes: 5 Erb (first trip 9:40 am); 3 Ottawa South (first trip 8:30 am); 4 Glasgow-Margaret (first trip 8:30 am); 1 Queen-River (first trip 8:00 am); 7 King (first trip 8:00 am); 16 Strasburg-Belmont (first trip 7:47 am); 6 Bridge-Courtland (first trip 7:45 am); 20 Victoria-Frederick (first trip 7:19 am). Largest groups: around King / Young (16,146); around Margaret / Guelph (3,798); around Victoria / Iron Horse Trail (2,176); around Highland / Queen (542).

gaps.title: Sunday 8 am: 1,615 people (6%) can't reach a hospital within 45 minutes by transit and walking
gaps.detail: Travel time is the median over departures from 8:00 am to 8:25 am on Sunday 15 November 2026, including walking to and from stops. 0 of these people have no stop within 800 m. Largest groups: around Margaret / Guelph (1,615). People reaching each one within 45 minutes: WRHN @ Queen’s Blvd. 23,096 (87%); WRHN @ Midtown 24,946 (94%); Cambridge Memorial Hospital 0 (0%).

fixes.title: Start route 6 Bridge-Courtland by 6:30 am on Sundays
fixes.benefit: 18,364 people near this route have no other bus or train within 800 m before 6:30 am (first trip now 7:45 am, last trip 11:45 pm). Shift workers, early hospital and retail staff and people coming home late gain most.
fixes.tradeoff: About 6 more trips and roughly 5 more bus-hours each Sunday at early hours, when fewer people ride, so the cost per rider is higher. GRT's cost per service hour would turn these hours into dollars; the buses and drivers have to come from new money or from other routes, which would then run less often.

method: Earliest arrival by the Connection Scan Algorithm (Dibbelt, Pajor, Strasser and Wagner, "Intriguingly Simple and Fast Transit Routing", SEA 2013; ACM JEA 2018) over one service day of Grand River Transit's published GTFS schedules (buses and ION light rail). From each 400 m grid cell of homes (2021 census population by dissemination area, shared evenly over the cells inside it), the rider walks at 4.8 km/h along 1.3x the straight-line distance to any stop within 800 m, rides, may change vehicles (60 s at the same stop, or a walk to another stop within 300 m), and walks from a stop within 800 m to the destination (or walks directly if it is within 800 m). Travel time is the median over departures every 5 minutes for half an hour from each scenario time. A destination type counts as reached when its nearest one is within 45 minutes. Shares are of people, not places. Stop gaps come from the timetable: first departure after 6:30 am, last before 11 pm, and fewer than two departures in the hour around the scenario time (all routes at the stop together). Fixes are ranked by the people living within 800 m of the changed stops who lack that service today; trip and bus-hour estimates come from the timetable's own trip times.
limits: Origins are 400 m grid cells with 2021 census population shared evenly within each dissemination area; real homes cluster differently, and rural areas (under 150 people per km²) count from their area's centre. Population is 2021; newer housing is missing.

Walking uses straight-line distance times 1.3, not the street network: rivers, highways, rail lines and missing sidewalks can make real walks much longer. No allowance for winter, slopes or mobility devices.

Schedules are the published timetable for one weekday (Tuesday 17 November 2026) and one Sunday (Sunday 15 November 2026); delays, detours, crowding and missed connections are not modelled. Saturday is not computed.

Destinations come from OpenStreetMap and may be missing or out of date; a clinic or pharmacy may not serve everyone (walk-in hours, specialties). Hospital means an OSM hospital not tagged emergency=no (three sites in the region); a hospital's other services and specialties are not distinguished.

Headway at a stop counts all routes together, so two routes going different ways can look like one frequent service. Routes outside the area that riders transfer to are included in travel times but not in fixes.

Fixes are candidates computed from the timetable, not GRT proposals. People helped counts residents near the changed stops, not expected riders. Bus-hour estimates count trip time only; layovers, deadheading and fleet limits are not included, and no dollar cost is given because no cost per hour was taken from a cited source.
MobilityPLUS, GRT's specialized service, and any on-demand or school services are not in the GTFS and are not counted.

legend.access: Each square is a 400 m grid cell (a point is a rural census area's centre). pop = 2021 residents (census population shared evenly over the cells of each dissemination area). <type>_<scenario> (types: hospital, grocery) = median minutes by transit and walking to the nearest destination of that type (null = not within 90 minutes). essentials_<scenario> = minutes until a grocery store, a pharmacy and a clinic are all reachable. Scenarios: w8 = Weekday 8 am, w22 = Weekday 10 pm, s8 = Sunday 8 am.
legend.stops: name and routes from GTFS. h_<scenario> = minutes between departures in the hour around that time, all routes together (null = none). first_/last_ wk (weekday) and su (Sunday) = first and last departure. gaps (when present) = late-start (first trip after 06:30 on a weekday or Sunday), early-end (last trip before 23:00), low-frequency (h over 30 at a scenario time).
legend.destinations: people_<scenario> = people in this area who reach it within 45 minutes. Destinations © OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database Licence (ODbL) 1.0, https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright; one Overpass query, retrieved 2026-11-14.
legend.gaps: One point per largest group of affected people for each gap (gap = the gap id).
